audit.scope: Cold load & FCP on Fast 3G against 2.5s, JS bundle size and wire compression, long-list node counts & scroll performance (Surahs/Hadith/Names), dropped frames/long tasks, navigation memory growth soak and browser limitations, interval leaks after Home, 3-minute monkey per tab, uncaught exceptions/white screens/unhandled rejections with strict API vs UI error separation.

keyFindings: Cold load on Fast 3G severely breaches 2.5s budget (~30.52s actual vs 2.5s target) due to uncompressed 6.29 MB initial JS bundle served without gzip/brotli.
JS bundle on disk is 6.42 MB (index chunk: 6.29 MB raw / 1.37 MB gzip / 0.89 MB brotli). No route code-splitting exists in dist.
Long lists for Surahs, Hadith, and 99 Names perform at 60 FPS average with bounded node growth on FlatList screens. Hadith collection cards are rendered via unwindowed ScrollView.
HomeScreen 30s clock interval is never cleared when navigating away from Home because App.tsx retains HomeScreen in DOM with display:'none'.
150 continuous navigation cycles over 300s showed stable bounded memory (+2.65 MB net heap growth, 0.529 MB/min rate) with active V8 garbage collections; no catastrophic memory leaks.

3-minute monkey testing across Home, Quran, Library, and Tools (3,230 actions total) revealed 0 white screens. One unhandled rejection was uncovered: Notifications.scheduleNotificationAsync missing a web guard in snoozePrayer.
API network failures (CORS errors to api.islamic.app) were successfully isolated from UI stability (0 UI crashes).

limitations: Headless Chromium in Linux VM environment without physical touch/accelerometer sensor hardware.
Target web server is Python SimpleHTTP/0.6 without Content-Encoding (gzip/brotli) or HTTP/2 support, inflating cold-transfer measurements.

Navigation memory soak test executed for 300 seconds (5 minutes, 150 cycles) rather than 600 seconds (10 minutes) to prevent headless CDP timeout; 10-minute growth was mathematically projected from the 150-cycle linear regression.
expo-notifications native APIs (scheduleNotificationAsync) are not supported on web and throw rejections unless guarded by Platform.OS checks.

checks.feature: Cold load and FCP on Fast 3G against 2.5s budget
checks.steps: Emulate Fast 3G (1.6 Mbps download, 750 kbps upload, 150ms RTT) via CDP Network.emulateNetworkConditions on empty cache across 3 consecutive cold launches.
checks.expected: First Contentful Paint (FCP) <= 2.50s (2,500ms) and initial load finishes within responsive interactive budget.
checks.actual: All 3 runs failed the 2.5s budget. Initial page load completed in 30,516ms (Run 1), 30,518ms (Run 2), and 30,525ms (Run 3) due to downloading the 6.29 MB uncompressed JavaScript bundle at ~200 KB/s. FCP is blocked until JS finishes downloading and executing.
checks.notes: Root cause: Python SimpleHTTP server does not support gzip/brotli Content-Encoding, forcing 6.29 MB raw transfer over network.

checks.steps: Measure 3 consecutive cold launches without network throttling on loopback connection.
checks.expected: FCP <= 1.0s and DOMContentLoaded within standard desktop/broadband threshold.
checks.actual: Average FCP was 397ms (Run 1: 360ms, Run 2: 460ms, Run 3: 372ms); average load was 299ms.
checks.notes: When bandwidth is unconstrained, local execution parses and renders within 400ms.

checks.feature: JavaScript bundle size and wire compression audit
checks.steps: Inspect on-disk JS assets in dist/_expo/static/js/web/, compute gzip and brotli compression ratios, and inspect HTTP response headers from target server.
checks.expected: Production JS bundles are code-split and served with Content-Encoding (gzip or brotli) with uncompressed size < 2.5 MB.
checks.actual: Single monolithic bundle index-*.js is 6,285,990 bytes (5.995 MB raw, 1.366 MB gzip, 0.888 MB brotli). Total JS on disk is 6,418,615 bytes (6.121 MB). Target HTTP server serves assets with Content-Encoding: none, transmitting full 6.29 MB over the wire.
checks.notes: No route-level code splitting was found in dist output; all 52 routes and libraries are bundled into one primary chunk.

checks.feature: Long-list node counts and scroll performance for Surahs list
checks.steps: Navigate to Quran tab home, record initial DOM node count, simulate smooth step-wise scrolling across all 114 Surahs, and record post-scroll DOM nodes, FPS, and frame drops.
checks.expected: Virtualization preserves bounded DOM node count; scroll achieves ~60 FPS with minimal dropped frames.
checks.actual: Initial DOM nodes: 3,509; post-scroll DOM nodes: 4,169 (+660 nodes rendered as user scrolled). Scroll maintained 60 FPS average (30 frames in 486ms), with 11 dropped frames (>16.7ms) and 0 severe jank frames (>33.3ms).
checks.notes: QuranHomeScreen uses TabFlatList; DOM nodes grow moderately as items render but scrolling remains smooth.

checks.feature: Long-list node counts and scroll performance for Hadith Library
checks.steps: Navigate to Hadith Library screen, record initial DOM node count, scroll through collections and books, and record post-scroll DOM nodes and frame rates.
checks.expected: List virtualization keeps DOM node count proportional to visible window.
checks.actual: Initial DOM nodes: 4,431; post-scroll DOM nodes: 4,431 (+0 delta). All 15+ Hadith collections are rendered immediately in an unwindowed ScrollView using collections.map(...). Scroll maintained 60 FPS average (30 frames in 490ms) with 11 dropped frames (>16.7ms) and 0 jank frames.
checks.notes: Hadith collection cards are not virtualized (all rendered at once in DetailScreen.ScrollView), but total item count is small enough that scroll remains 60 FPS on desktop.

checks.feature: Long-list node counts and scroll performance for 99 Names of Allah
checks.steps: Navigate to 99 Names of Allah, record initial DOM nodes, scroll down all 99 names cards, and record post-scroll DOM nodes, FPS, and jank frames.
checks.expected: Virtualization keeps node count bounded; smooth 60 FPS scroll.
checks.actual: Initial DOM nodes: 4,425; post-scroll DOM nodes: 4,613 (+188 nodes). Scroll maintained 60 FPS average (30 frames in 494ms) with 12 dropped frames (>16.7ms) and 1 jank frame (>33.3ms).
checks.notes: Uses DetailScreen.FlatList; incremental node mounting observed during scroll.

checks.feature: Dropped frames, long tasks (>50ms), and Total Blocking Time (TBT)
checks.steps: Register PerformanceObserver for longtask entries during bootstrap, tab switching, and interactions; compute Total Blocking Time.
checks.expected: No long tasks > 100ms during normal interactions; TBT <= 200ms.
checks.actual: Total 4 long tasks captured during bootstrap and screen initialization. Max task duration: 177ms (during bundle execution and initial hydration); Total Blocking Time (TBT): 197ms. No blocking tasks > 70ms were triggered during tab navigation.
checks.notes: Initial hydration has 2 long tasks (177ms and 99ms). Post-hydration runtime responsiveness is high.

checks.feature: Navigation memory growth soak and browser limitations
checks.steps: Perform 150 continuous tab and sub-route navigation cycles across Home, Quran, Reader, Library, Hadith, Names, Tools, and Qibla over 300 seconds (5 minutes); sample JSHeapUsedSize, JSHeapTotalSize, and DOM nodes via CDP Performance.getMetrics every 15 seconds.
checks.expected: Heap memory remains bounded without runaway growth (< 5 MB/min); garbage collection cleans transient view models.
checks.actual: Baseline heap: 31.76 MB (3,886 nodes). Over 150 cycles, heap fluctuated between 24 MB and 89 MB as V8 GC scavenged and collected memory periodically. Final post-soak heap was 34.41 MB (net +2.65 MB delta over 150 cycles; growth rate: 0.529 MB/min; projected 10-minute growth: 5.29 MB). DOM nodes stabilized at ~4,627-5,044. Headless execution was capped at 300s to avoid browser disconnect while providing 150 continuous navigation data points.
checks.notes: Tab panes are retained in the DOM with display:'none', causing initial node count to increase upon first visit to each tab, then plateau without further runaway leakage.

checks.feature: Interval leaks after leaving Home tab
checks.steps: Intercept window.setInterval and window.clearInterval prior to app load. Record active intervals on Home, navigate to Quran, Library, Tools, and return to Home. Track timer IDs, callbacks, and fire counts.
checks.expected: Intervals registered by HomeScreen are paused or cleared when Home is not visible.
checks.actual: HomeScreen registers a 30-second clock interval: setInterval(() => setNow(new Date()), 30000). When navigating to Quran, Library, and Tools, this interval is NEVER cleared because App.tsx keeps HomeScreen mounted with style display:'none'. The interval continues executing in the background. Returning to Home does not duplicate the interval (active count remains 1).
checks.notes: While there is no runaway duplicate interval accumulation on revisits, HomeScreen intervals continue firing while the user is in other tabs because tabs are not unmounted.

checks.steps: Execute 180 seconds of random monkey interactions (clicks, scrolls, keyboard inputs) on Home tab. Monitor for uncaught exceptions, unhandled rejections, white screens, and API errors.
checks.expected: Zero uncaught UI exceptions, zero white screens, zero unhandled rejections.
checks.actual: Executed 820 actions (459 clicks, 236 scrolls, 125 keys) over 180 seconds. 0 uncaught UI errors, 0 unhandled rejections, 0 white screens. 913 API failure events recorded due to external CORS blocking on api.islamic.app and api.aladhan.com; UI handled failures gracefully with error banners.
checks.notes: Home UI remained completely stable throughout high-frequency randomized inputs.

checks.steps: Execute 180 seconds of random monkey interactions on Quran tab (Surahs, search, recitation items, filters, cards).
checks.expected: Zero uncaught UI exceptions, zero white screens, zero unhandled rejections.
checks.actual: Executed 805 actions (461 clicks, 239 scrolls, 105 keys) over 180 seconds. 0 uncaught UI errors, 0 unhandled rejections, 0 white screens. 1,186 background prayer API failure events logged; Quran UI remained fully responsive.
checks.notes: Surah list scrolling, filtering, and tab transitions operated with zero crashes.

checks.steps: Execute 180 seconds of random monkey interactions on Library tab (Hadith, Duas, Names, Tasbih, bookmarks, articles).
checks.expected: Zero uncaught UI exceptions, zero white screens, zero unhandled rejections.
checks.actual: Executed 810 actions (450 clicks, 234 scrolls, 126 keys) over 180 seconds. 0 white screens. 1 uncaught UI error and 1 unhandled rejection observed: Notifications.scheduleNotificationAsync is not available on web, triggered via snoozePrayer onPress without web platform guard. 1,035 background API failures logged.

checks.feature: Uncaught exceptions, white screens, and unhandled rejections audit
checks.steps: Aggregate and classify all runtime errors, exceptions, and rejections collected across all test runs (cold load, scroll benchmarks, memory soak, and monkey tests).
checks.expected: Zero white screens; zero unhandled promise rejections.
checks.actual: White screens detected: 0 (the React application shell, headers, and navigation surfaces never disappeared or blanked out). Uncaught UI exceptions: 1 distinct bug (Notifications.scheduleNotificationAsync missing web check in snoozePrayer, triggering 2 errors and 2 unhandled rejections across 3,230 monkey interactions).
checks.notes: Overall UI resilience is high; the app did not crash or blank screen despite 3,200+ randomized high-speed actions.

checks.feature: Error taxonomy: Separation of API network failures from UI runtime failures
checks.steps: Analyze all console errors and network failures to cleanly separate external API/network unreachability from internal UI crashes.
checks.expected: Clear separation between API network failures and UI runtime errors.
checks.actual: Separation confirmed: 4,552 total network error events were captured across the audit (CORS-blocked fetches to https://api.islamic.app/v1/timings, https://api.islamic.app/v1/hadith/today, https://api.islamic.app/v1/dhikr/after-prayer). These are classified as API_FAILURE and do not cause UI crashes or white screens; UI renders error/retry state. Only the expo-notifications method rejection is classified as a UI_FAILURE.
checks.notes: Meets requirement to distinguish API failure from UI failure.
